headline: Landslide threat: Sajek Valley tourism halted indefinitely
summary: The Rangamati district administration has closed all tourist centers in Sajek Valley due to relentless rain and the risk of landslides.
details: The Rangamati district administration has announced the indefinite closure of all tourist centers in Sajek Valley. The decision comes after several days of relentless heavy rainfall increased the risk of landslides in the hilly region.
caption:
Heavy rains and landslide risks have forced the closure of Sajek Valley. All tourist activities are now banned until further notice.

headline_marked: Dhaka ranks [[third least livable city]] globally, behind only war-torn Damascus and Tripoli
headline: Dhaka ranks third least livable city globally, behind only war-torn Damascus and Tripoli
summary: The Economist Intelligence Unit's 2026 Global Liveability Index ranks Dhaka 171st out of 173 cities, scoring 42 out of 100.
details: Dhaka has been ranked as the third least livable city in the world according to the Economist Intelligence Unit's (EIU) 2026 Global Liveability Index. Out of 173 cities evaluated, Dhaka ranks 171st, placing it just above war-torn Damascus, Syria, and Tripoli, Libya.

The index evaluates cities based on five key categories: stability, healthcare, culture and environment, education, and infrastructure. Dhaka scored a total of 42 out of 100, which is just above the 'unbearable' threshold of 40.

Infrastructure was the city's lowest-scoring category, receiving a score of only 27. This metric includes road networks, public transport quality, and the availability of housing, energy, water, and telecommunications.

Education was Dhaka's highest-scoring sector, receiving a score of 67. Other categories included stability (45), healthcare (42), and culture and environment (41), which considers factors like corruption, social restrictions, and climate.

Other cities at the bottom of the index include Karachi, Algiers, Lagos, Port Moresby, Kyiv, Harare, and Tehran. Conversely, the top 10 most livable cities include Copenhagen, Vienna, Melbourne, and Sydney.
The report notes that a score above 80 is considered acceptable, while a score below 40 is deemed unbearable. Dhaka's score of 42 puts it near the bottom of thelargest global urban centers.
